references_named: CSS Color Module Level 4 named colours (W3C)
rationale: The work cleanly enacts Richter's chance-ordered colour chart by handing authorship to a W3C committee and the visitor's own rendering engine. The mechanism (backgroundColor + getComputedStyle readback, per-visit shuffle, no persistence) is the argument: the artist mixed nothing, chose nothing, and did not decide the count. The rebeccapurple memorial detail and the absurd committee names give it double-coding depth. It is materially distinct from the catalogue — Richter is a new reference, and the readymade-of-a-spec angle is fresh.
reservations: The chance/order axis is real but lightly staged; the 'order' pole is just the alphabetical list, which is a thin version of Richter's systematic mixing. The piece is also visually quiet — closer to a tool than a gag — so the surface wit is gentler than most catalogue entries.
revision_suggestion: Consider seeding the shuffle from a non-obvious source (e.g., the visitor's locale, the time, or a hash of the names themselves) so the chance axis feels more pointed, and add a one-line wall-label-style caption that names the price/medium in the catalogue manner to land the P6 critique more visibly.
